facts.statement: Hoplitosaurus was an armored dinosaur genus related to Polacanthus.
facts.quote: Hoplitosaurus (meaning "Hoplite lizard") was a genus of armored dinosaur related to Polacanthus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen USNM 4752 was discovered in 1898 by Nelson Horatio Darton near Buffalo Gap Station.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, USNM 4752, was discovered in 1898 by Nelson Horatio Darton, near Buffalo Gap Station

facts.statement: Frederic Augustus Lucas briefly described the material in 1901 as a new species of Stegosaurus before assigning it to its own genus.
facts.quote: Frederic Augustus Lucas described it briefly in 1901 as a new species of Stegosaurus, but soon gave the material its own genus.

facts.statement: Charles W. Gilmore fully described the material in 1914.
facts.quote: Charles W. Gilmore fully described the material in 1914.

facts.statement: Hoplitosaurus lived during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous in the Lakota Formation of Custer County, South Dakota.
facts.quote: It was named from a partial skeleton found in the Barremian (Early Cretaceous) Lakota Formation of Custer County, South Dakota.

facts.statement: Hoplitosaurus lived approximately 130 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 130 millones de años, en el Barremiense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Hoplitosaurus lived from the Barremian to the Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Gilmore described Hoplitosaurus as being about 1.2 meters (4 feet) tall at the hips.
facts.quote: Gilmore described the animal as being about 1.2 m (4 ft) tall at the hips.

facts.statement: According to Gilmore, Hoplitosaurus reached a height of 1.2 meters at the hips and a length of around 5 meters.
facts.quote: según Gilmore llegó a medir 1,2 metros de alto a las caderas y un largo de alrededor de 5 metros.

facts.statement: Hoplitosaurus was a quadrupedal herbivore that ate low to the ground, using its armor as its main defense.
facts.quote: It would have been a quadrupedal herbivore, eating low to the ground; armor was its main defense.

facts.statement: It would have been a quadrupedal herbivore eating close to the ground, with armor serving as its primary defense.
facts.quote: Habría sido un herbívoro cuadrúpedo, comiendo a ras del piso, con la armadura como su defensa principal.

facts.statement: Hoplitosaurus is classified within the family Nodosauridae.
Hoplitosaurus belongs to the subfamily Polacanthinae.
Today, Hoplitosaurus is considered either a polacanthine or polacanthid ankylosaur depending on classification preference.
facts.quote: Today, both are considered to be polacanthine or polacanthid ankylosaurs, depending on classification preference

facts.statement: William T. Blows and Javier Pereda-Suberbiola considered Hoplitosaurus to be synonymous with Polacanthus, but this view has since been rejected.
facts.quote: William T. Blows and Javier Pereda-Suberbiola both considered the genus to be the same as Polacanthus, creating the new combination Polacanthus marshii, but this has since been rejected.

facts.statement: Ken Carpenter and James Kirkland noted that similarities between Hoplitosaurus and Polacanthus were either widespread among ankylosaurs or based on bone damage.
facts.quote: Ken Carpenter and James Kirkland noted that many of the resemblances between the two were more widely distributed among ankylosaurs than previously thought, or were based on damage to the bones

facts.statement: A point of discussion regarding Hoplitosaurus is the lack of a clear tail club, as it possessed prominent dorsal spines and tips rather than the club structure seen in Polacanthus.
facts.quote: Un punto de discusión resultó ser la falsa porra de la cola. En el Polacanthus, éste resulta de una interpretación de vértebras caudales, de tendones osificados, y armadura, no estando claro en que se basa el informe en Hoplitosaurus, que tenía espinas dorsales y puntas muy prominentes.

facts.statement: Hoplitosaurus is an obscure genus that has been subject to misinterpretation due to damaged remains.
facts.quote: It is an obscure genus which has been subject to some misinterpretation of its damaged remains.
